thread.title: Apple (AAPL) 3rd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Apple (AAPL) 3rd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect
text:
Shutterstock photo
Can a strong Apple ( AAPL ) earnings report and confident guidance stop the decline in tech stocks?
Fresh on the heels of sprucing up its hardware line with new Macs and iPads, Apple will report earnings results after the closing bell Thursday. Apple is the only remaining FAANG — Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) — that has yet to report, and what the company reveals Thursday could be the catalyst the market needs to reverse the downward spiral investors have experienced.
In the three months that ended September, Wall Street expect the Cupertino, Calif.-based tech giant to earn $2.78 per share on revenue of $61.59 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $2.07 per share on revenue of $52.58 billion. For the full year, earnings are expected to rise 29% year over year to $11.79 per share, while full-year revenue of $264.03 billion would rise 15.2% year over year.
Apple shares have held up much better than most tech stocks during the recent selloff. The shares have actually risen some 13% in the past three months, compared to the 5% decline in the S&P 500 index during that same span. And much of Apple’s strength has been due to the company’s stellar earnings track record.
It’s likely for this reason Wedbush Securities analyst Daniel Ives last week noted Apple shares can reach $310, assigning Apple with the highest price estimate on the Street, suggesting some 45% upside from current levels of around $213. How quickly Apple can reach that target depends on how many iPhones, particularly the more expensive iPhone X models, Apple sold during the quarter. Ives believes that about 350 million iPhones could be upgraded in the next 12-18 months.
The Street will be looking for fourth quarter iPhone unit sales of 47 million, which would market a 1% increased year over year. And this is where higher average selling prices (ASP) will provide a boost to revenue despite the meager unit growth. The company, as recent as September, introduced the new iPhone XR, iPhone XS, and iPhone XS Max. Contribution from these three new models will be minimal. But the bet is on the all-important holiday quarter when those devices are expected to pay huge dividends.
On Thursday analysts will also focus on Apple’s sales figures in China — its second largest market. Reports of the recent decline of the Chinese Yuan, which makes iPhones in China more expensive, has been a concern. In the third quarter, Apple experience sequential declines in revenue across all geographic regions. Sales in Greater China came in at $9.55 billion, which was down 27% on the quarter but up 19% on the year. It remains to be seen what impact the Chinese Yuan and the tariffs will have on this quarter.
Services revenue, which has a current run rate of $33.4 billion and includes Apple Music, the App Store and Apple Pay, will be another area of focus. Third quarter Services revenue surged 31% year over year to the all-time high $9.55 billion, topping the $9.2 billion analysts were looking for. Another solid showing in the Services segment, combined with stronger APS’s, should affirm the strong relative support the share price has already demonstrated.
